equation_summary.state_vector: x = [T1, T2, T3, omega_UW, omega_Nip, omega_RW]

paper_source.title: Equation Identifier for Practical system identification for roll-to-roll web tension control
paper_source.scope: Equations, definitions, decision rules, and examples extracted only from the supplied PDF.
paper_source.typography: Times-style body text with Cambria Math/TeX-like math extraction; dominant extracted size is about 9-10 pt.

equation_summary.section2_note: Paper-facing equations are taken from the supplied PDF paper1_isa_v2_equation_identifier.pdf. The PDF contains numbered equations (1)-(9) plus important unnumbered definitions labeled U-*. Tokens such as CS-BO(30), WS-BO(30), HGS+BO(5), and HGS+BO(10) are method labels or evaluation budgets, not equation numbers. System equations show the reduced equations actually used by the dashboard backend.

paper_equations.title: Plant variables and physical setup
paper_equations.equation: x = [T1, T2, T3, omega_UW, omega_Nip, omega_RW]^T in R^6; u = [u_UW, u_Nip, u_RW]^T; y = [T1, T2, T3]^T; EA = E*h*w; v_i = omega_i*R_i; J_reel proportional R^4
paper_equations.variables: x contains three span tensions and three roller angular velocities; u is the paper motor-torque input; y is measured tension; EA is axial web stiffness.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF uses these definitions to set the three-span R2R plant and to motivate the seven-parameter SysID vector.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend uses the same state and output order. Its input vector is a held motor-voltage command that is converted through backend motor gains.

paper_equations.title: Web tension dynamics
paper_equations.variables: T_i: span tension, EA: axial web stiffness, L_i: span length, v_i: roller surface velocity.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF states the boundary condition T_0 = T_4 = 0 and links this tension equation to RK4 integration, one-step residuals, and the logging-rate result.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend reduced model keeps the velocity-mismatch stiffness term and adds reference-tension relaxation instead of the convective transport term.

paper_equations.title: Roller velocity dynamics
paper_equations.variables: R_i: roller radius, J_i: moment of inertia, f_i: viscous friction, u_i: motor torque input.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF uses this roller equation to explain why J drift is dominant: J appears in the tension-coupling, friction, and torque coefficients.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend state uses omega_i, so the runnable model represents this balance as domega_i/dt with web torque, friction, inertia, and voltage-to-torque gain.

paper_equations.title: Outer-loop tension PI velocity correction
paper_equations.equation: v_corr,i = (L_i/EA)Kp_star [sigma_i e_i + (1/TI) integral_0^t sigma_i e_i(tau) d tau]; omega_ref,i = omega_ss,i + v_corr,i/R_i
paper_equations.variables: e_i = T_ref,i - T_meas,i; sigma_i in {-1,+1,+1}; Kp_star = Kp*EA/L is the normalized proportional gain.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF emphasizes that L/EA in this controller cancels EA/L in equation (1), making Kp_star the practical information-content knob.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend controller uses the same tension-error-to-velocity-correction concept with a reduced coupling map for the three rollers.

paper_equations.title: Inner-loop velocity P plus feedforward torque
paper_equations.equation: u_i = K_vel,i(omega_ref,i - omega_i) + u_ff,i; K_vel,i = alpha*J_i*omega_n,i; omega_n,i = sqrt(EA*R_i^2/(J_i*L_i)); alpha = 1.4
paper_equations.variables: omega_ref,i is the target from equation (3); omega_i is measured roller speed; u_ff,i is the feedforward torque.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF links this cascade loop to the loss of predictive value in zeta_CL,min and the practical use of Kp_star instead.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend uses a velocity PI plus feedforward torque, then converts torque to a clamped voltage command.

paper_equations.title: Measurement-based feedforward
paper_equations.equation: u_ff,i = +/- T_meas*R_i + f_i*omega_i; u_ff = [T0*R0, (T2 - T1)R1, -T2*R2]^T + f o omega
paper_equations.variables: The sign depends on roller/span direction; f o omega denotes elementwise friction compensation.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF states that measurement-based feedforward compensates measured tension load and friction and can absorb some EA drift.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend feedforward uses the current web-torque balance and friction term to reduce the burden on the feedback loops.

paper_equations.title: Ratio-parameter SysID formulation
paper_equations.equation: k_t,i = R_i^2/J_i; k_f,i = f_i/J_i; k_u,i = R_i/J_i; theta = [kt_UW, kt_Nip, kt_RW, kf_UW, kf_Nip, kf_RW, EA] in R^7
paper_equations.variables: R_i and L_i are treated as known measurable constants; ku_i can be derived rather than estimated independently.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF uses these ratio parameters because they are the combinations that appear in equation (2).
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend estimates the same seven displayed parameter names, while its runnable kt values are voltage-to-torque gains in the reduced model.

paper_equations.title: One-step prediction-error cost
paper_equations.variables: y_k is the measured tension vector at the logging instant; yhat_k(theta) is the model prediction.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF identifies this as the central SysID objective and uses it to explain the sensitivity to logging period and filtering.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The dashboard reports parameter-estimation error tables and RMSE_theta from the resulting estimates.

paper_equations.title: Multi-condition prediction-error cost
paper_equations.variables: c indexes distinct excitation or operating conditions.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF states that multi-condition residuals add independent constraints and reduce shallow or ambiguous cost landscapes.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The excitation validation tab compares which excitation profiles produce better SysID information.

paper_equations.title: Initial guesses and SysID accuracy metrics
paper_equations.equation: theta_init = alpha*theta_true, alpha in {1.5, 2, 5, 10, 50}; error_j = |theta_est,j - theta_true,j|/theta_true,j*100; RMSE_theta = n^-1 sum_i |(theta_hat_i - theta_i)/theta_i|*100; RMSE_y = n^-1 sum_i RMSE_i
paper_equations.variables: alpha scales the initial guess; error_j is per-parameter relative error; RMSE_theta and RMSE_y aggregate SysID and tracking errors.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF uses these metrics to compare convergence basins, data designs, and validation step responses.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The backend reports RMSE_theta as a root-mean-square relative error, so the dashboard labels it as the implementation aggregate.

paper_equations.title: Channel-weighted retuning score
paper_equations.equation: S = sum_{i=1}^n w_i (RMSE_i/1 + OS_i/100 + t90_i/15 + U_total,i/200); w_i = |Delta T_ref,i|/sum_j |Delta T_ref,j|; RMSE_i = sqrt(N^-1 sum_k (T_i(t_k) - T_ref,i)^2); OS_i = max(0, (T_i,peak - T_ref,i,new)/|Delta T_ref,i|)*100; U_total,i = integral_0^Tsim u_i^2(t) dt
paper_equations.variables: S combines tracking error, overshoot, rise time to 90%, and total squared control effort.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF links this score to Table 3/Figure 10 and the HGS+BO(5) result: median cost 0.342 with five real evaluations versus CS-BO(30) at 0.407.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: The dashboard retuning study uses a related cost combining RMSE, overshoot, t90, and control effort.

paper_equations.title: Deployment rules derived from the equations
paper_equations.equation: tau_min = 1/max_i(|Re(lambda_i)|); NF: tau_min/Tlog >= 5; SN: Tlog = 10-20 ms and LPF fc >= 50 Hz; Kp_star = 100 default, Kp_star = 200 under high noise; validate RMSE_y < epsilon and S < C_target
paper_equations.variables: NF: noise-free; SN: sensor-noise case; LPF: low-pass filter; Kp_star controls transient information content.
paper_equations.paper_use: The PDF describes these as decision rules derived from the model, SysID objective, and retuning score, not new governing equations.
paper_equations.dashboard_note: Validation tabs expose the logging, excitation, SysID, and retuning checks that correspond to these rules.

backend_equations.title: Web transport kinematics
backend_equations.variables: R_i: roller radius, omega_i: angular velocity, v_i: surface speed.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used in simulation logging, tension derivatives, and SysID EA regression.

backend_equations.title: Reduced three-span tension dynamics
backend_equations.equation: dT1/dt = (EA/L1)(v_Nip - v_UW) - lambda_T(T1 - T1_ref); dT2/dt = (EA/L2)(v_RW - v_Nip) - lambda_T(T2 - T2_ref); dT3/dt = (EA/L3)(v_RW - 0.5(v_UW + v_Nip)) - lambda_T(T3 - T3_ref)
backend_equations.variables: EA: web stiffness, L_i: span length, lambda_T: relaxation rate, T_i_ref: target tension.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by tension_derivatives(), derivatives(), rk4_step(), simulation rows, and the Calculation tab derivative example.

backend_equations.title: Web torque balance on rollers
backend_equations.equation: tau_web,UW = (T3 - T1)R_UW; tau_web,Nip = (T1 - T2)R_Nip; tau_web,RW = (T2 - T3)R_RW
backend_equations.variables: T_i: span tensions, R_i: roller radii.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by roller dynamics and by the cascade PI feedforward torque.

backend_equations.title: Roller velocity dynamics
backend_equations.variables: J_i: inertia, kt_i: voltage-to-torque gain, kf_i: viscous friction, u_i: motor voltage.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by roller_velocity_derivatives(), derivatives(), rk4_step(), and SysID kt/kf regression.

backend_equations.title: Outer tension PI correction
backend_equations.equation: c_i = Kp_star*e_i + (Kp_star/TI)*integral(e_i dt),  e_i = T_ref,i - T_i
backend_equations.variables: c_i: tension-loop velocity correction, e_i: tension error, TI: integral time.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by CascadePIController.update() to build roller speed references.

backend_equations.title: Velocity reference coupling
backend_equations.equation: v_ref,UW = v_line - c1 - 0.5c3; v_ref,Nip = v_line + c1 - c2 - 0.5c3; v_ref,RW = v_line + c2 + c3; omega_ref,i = v_ref,i/R_i
backend_equations.variables: v_line: target line speed, c_i: tension-loop corrections.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by the PI controller to convert tension error into roller angular-speed references.

backend_equations.title: Inner velocity PI plus feedforward
backend_equations.equation: tau_cmd,i = Kvel*e_omega,i + (Kvel/TI_vel)*integral(e_omega,i dt) + tau_ff,i; tau_ff,i = kf_i*omega_ref,i - tau_web,i; u_i = clamp(tau_cmd,i/kt_i)
backend_equations.variables: e_omega,i = omega_ref,i - omega_i; tau_ff,i is friction and web-torque feedforward.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by CascadePIController.update() to produce the held motor-voltage input u.

backend_equations.title: RK4 state update
backend_equations.variables: k1...k4 are derivatives evaluated by the backend model while u is held constant over the integration step.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by rk4_step() for every 1 ms physics update in simulation.

backend_equations.title: Simulation tension RMSE
backend_equations.variables: N: logged row count, i: T1/T2/T3.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by compute_metrics() and displayed in Simulation, Drift, and Retuning results.

backend_equations.title: Control effort RMS
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by compute_metrics() and displayed in Simulation, Drift, and Retuning results.

backend_equations.title: SysID roller regression
backend_equations.variables: Finite differences from logged rows provide domega_i/dt.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by estimate_parameters() to solve kt_UW, kt_Nip, kt_RW, kf_UW, kf_Nip, and kf_RW.

backend_equations.title: SysID EA regression
backend_equations.variables: speed_strain_i is the backend span-speed mismatch for T1, T2, or T3.
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by estimate_parameters() to solve EA from logged simulation rows.

backend_equations.title: SysID parameter RMSE
backend_equations.backend_use: Used by estimate_parameters() and all SysID validation result tables.

derivation_steps: Step 1: Compute surface speeds from roller kinematics: v_i = R_i * omega_i.
Step 2: Use speed differences across spans to compute web strain-rate.
Step 3: Convert strain-rate into tension-rate with EA, then add the reduced-model relaxation term.
Step 4: Convert neighboring span tensions into web torque on each roller.
Step 5: Use motor torque kt_i*u_i, web torque, and friction kf_i*omega_i to compute roller acceleration.
Step 6: Concatenate all derivatives in state-vector order and advance the state with RK4.
Step 7: During SysID, rearrange the same one-step equations into least-squares form for the seven estimated parameters.

limitations: The PDFs do not provide raw simulation CSV files or optimization seeds.
The project reference contains plant-specific EA/regime metadata, but exact per-plant `R`, `J`, `f`, `L`, and `b` arrays are not available.
The dashboard backend uses the implemented reduced three-span state model documented in `backend/models/equations.py`; several paper equations are represented in reduced form.

Paper values are mostly medians across ten plants and many seeds; this rerun uses the baseline-compatible P01 plant for section experiments unless the existing retuning helper performs its own candidates.
